questions.q: What generally determines how much flexibility exists to change an order line?
options: The customer's industry
The day of the week the order was entered
How far the line has progressed through fulfillment
The number of lines on the order
questions.explain: The further a line has progressed — picked, shipped, invoiced — the fewer clean changes remain available.

questions.q: If a line has already shipped, how is a quantity reduction typically handled?
options: Through a return process, since the physical goods already exist at the customer's site
A simple quantity edit on the original order line
It cannot be handled at all, ever
By deleting the original sales order
questions.explain: Once goods have shipped, a reduction requires a return rather than an ordinary quantity change.

questions.q: What is the difference between changing a line and cancelling a line?
options: There is no difference
Cancelling is only possible for invoiced lines
A change always increases the price; a cancellation always decreases it
A change modifies a line that remains open; a cancellation closes it before it completes
questions.explain: A change keeps the line open with modified details; a cancellation closes the line before it ever completes.

questions.q: In the lesson's hypothetical, Harborview asks to reduce SO-48217 from 400 to 350 units before picking starts. What happens to the 5% volume discount?
options: It is removed because the quantity changed
It still applies, because 350 units still clears the 300-unit threshold
It doubles automatically
It requires a new credit check
questions.explain: 350 units is still at or above the 300-unit threshold for the automatic 5% discount rule, so it still applies.

questions.q: Once a sales order line has already been invoiced, what is required to correct it?
options: A simple edit to the original sales order line
Nothing — invoiced lines cannot ever be corrected
Action taken in Receivables, typically a credit memo
A new purchase order
questions.explain: Once invoiced, the Receivables transaction exists independently of the order, so correction happens in Receivables via a credit memo.
